clue.text: Short note — setter gets paper occasionally

indicators.note: short means the note's name is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: sol is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
in crosswords the setter refers to themself as me
The Times is a national newspaper

explanation.surface: A crossword setter dashes off a brief memo and now and then gets a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims SOL to SO; ME is the setter, as in many puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean now and then, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Pervert's feeling nauseous over nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes above it, so first

parts.note: feeling nauseous is being sick
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A depraved person is said to be queasy about nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: A sicko is slang for a person with perverted or sick tastes.

clue.text: In a second, maybe release policeman overseas

parts.note: 'in a mo' is everyday British for in a second, so mo stands for a second
to untie is one way to release, hence maybe

explanation.surface: Someone is about to release a policeman abroad any moment now.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'just a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, a lawman abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Spine on book wrongly identified as a flier?

parts.note: a thorn is a spine on a plant
ill as an adverb means badly or wrongly, as in ill-advised

explanation.surface: The spine of a book has been printed with a mistaken label about a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spine on book' suggests the back of a volume; it is a plant's spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A thornbill is a small bird, and birds fly, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One's unilateral in a surface sense

definitions.text: One's unilateral in a surface sense

parts.words: One's unilateral in a surface sense
parts.note: describes a band of paper given a half twist so that, as a surface, it has only one side

explanation.surface: Someone is said to act alone in a superficial way.
explanation.definitionFit: This twisted loop is the classic surface with only one face and one edge.

clue.text: Group finally misses the boat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A party of travellers turns up too late and misses the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection or group of things or people.

clue.text: Ditch bodyguard, captured by enemy

indicators.note: captured by means the bodyguard is held inside the word for enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard unit

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a protector who has been taken prisoner by the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning abandon; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a defensive trench or moat around a fortification.

clue.text: Dim female, commonly, is not

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial or nonstandard form of is not

explanation.surface: A woman who is not dim, as people say informally.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint and dim both mean barely visible or weak in light.

clue.text: Aramis badly cut by upper-class warrior

indicators.note: cut by means the jumbled name is split open by the next piece
badly signals that the letters of the musketeer's name are jumbled

parts.note: U is the British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Aramis, one of the Three Musketeers, is badly wounded by a posh swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ARAMIS to SAMRAI, and 'cut by' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Lady and gentleman meeting old king

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name
Bert is a man's name

explanation.surface: A lady and a gentleman have an audience with an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was an Anglo-Saxon ruler of Kent who accepted Christianity.

clue.text: Joule uncovered in search for another unit

indicators.note: in means the middle letters go inside the word for search

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: uncovered means the word loses its outer letters, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A physicist searches for a different unit after discovering the joule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joule' looks like part of the definition, but it is the word stripped of its outer letters; the definition is 'another unit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The coulomb is the SI measure of electric charge, another named unit like the joule.

clue.text: One stopping better horse's victory

indicators.note: stopping means the numeral plugs a gap inside the word for better

parts.note: to trump is to better or outdo
I is the Roman numeral for one
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A single person backing the better horse at the races wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like a punter; it is the verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great win or success.

clue.text: Frequently tone down after losing head

indicators.note: after losing head means the word for tone down drops its first letter

parts.note: to soften is to tone down

explanation.surface: Someone is told to moderate their tone repeatedly after losing their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently both mean many times.

clue.text: Delete content of unchristian sort of note that's monstrous

indicators.note: deleting a word's content leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: a natural is a musical note neither sharp nor flat

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out an unchristian kind of message as wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delete content of' empties UNCHRISTIAN, leaving its first and last letters, U and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural can mean abnormal and monstrous, against nature.

clue.text: Clue: funeral could result if this spills

definitions.text: Clue: funeral could result if this spills

indicators.note: the answer's letters, spilt and rearranged, would give the two words before it

explanation.surface: A warning that a spill of dangerous material could lead to a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards: the answer's eleven letters rearrange to CLUE FUNERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt radioactive reactor material could well cause deaths, hence a funeral.

clue.text: Section of weekend supplement

indicators.note: section of means a run of letters lies inside the word weekend

explanation.surface: Part of the Saturday newspaper's colour magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplement' looks like a newspaper extra; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out is to supplement or stretch a meagre supply.

clue.text: Girl stopping to make possible fun?

indicators.note: stopping means the girl's name plugs a gap inside the next phrase's synonym

parts.note: to enable is to make possible
Joy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl decides to stay so that the fun can go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enjoyable is pleasant, full of fun; the question mark flags noun standing for adjective.

clue.text: It should put an end to cricket

definitions.text: It should put an end to cricket

parts.words: It should put an end to cricket
parts.note: the cricket meant is the chirping creature, not the game, and the product kills it

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for the end of the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket, the British summer sport, is the bait; the target is a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect-killing sprays end the life of crickets and other bugs.

clue.text: Purity within new and old church? New church

parts.note: within means in
CE is the Church of England
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A question about whether purity lies in a modern or traditional church, answered with a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is freedom from sin or guilt, moral purity.

clue.text: In prison I unravel novel — Dracula's favourite bit?

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An inmate in jail unpicks the plot of a novel about a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges I UNRAVEL to ULARVEIN; 'novel' looks like Bram Stoker's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires like Dracula bite the neck, where this big blood vessel runs.

clue.text: Girl's clothing by boy's cheek, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase before it is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Jim is a boy's name and a lip is cheek or insolence, giving Jim's lip

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's uniform draws backchat from a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once worn by British schoolgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: This pinafore dress was standard girls' school uniform in Britain.

clue.text: She's spiteful, upsetting the apple cart up front

indicators.note: upsetting means the picked letters are turned the other way round
up front picks the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A nasty woman spoils everyone's plans by upsetting the apple cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' gives T, A, C, and 'upsetting' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat is slang for a spiteful, malicious woman.

clue.text: Shame of king once breaking into many shops

indicators.note: breaking into means the royal letters go inside the word for many shops

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops under one owner
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a former king

explanation.surface: A former monarch disgraced himself by burgling a string of stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is distress or vexation from humiliation, a sense of shame.

clue.text: When not to eat up my pork I pickled!

indicators.note: pickled means mixed up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about pickling pork instead of eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' rearranges UP MY PORK I; pork is doubly off-limits on this Jewish holy day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Day of Atonement is the Jewish holy day marked by a full fast.

clue.text: Particularly hard sarcasm

definitions.meaning: like a metal in hardness, an adjective formed with a -y ending
saying the opposite of what is meant, often mockingly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both metal-like in hardness and dry mockery through contrary meaning.

clue.text: Money's left inside jar

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left goes within the word for money

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Coins have been left in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot; it is the verb, to grate or conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash is to conflict or jar with something.

clue.text: Desire tea, to finish off after hot dog? Sort of

indicators.note: after means these pieces come behind the letter for hot

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a yen is a longing or desire

indicators.note: to finish off picks the closing letter of the word tea

explanation.surface: Someone craves a cup of tea to round off a hot dog snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dog' reads as a sausage snack; 'to finish off' takes the last letter of TEA, A.
explanation.definitionFit: This African scavenger looks rather like a dog, though not one strictly, hence 'sort of'.

clue.text: Everyone dividing benefit is swell

indicators.note: dividing means the word for everyone splits the word for benefit

parts.note: a boon is a benefit
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Sharing out an advantage among everyone is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like an adjective, great; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell or inflate rapidly.

clue.text: Intellect almost raised game

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: mind means intellect

explanation.surface: A brainy person nearly brought up a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MIND to MIN, which 'raised' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nim is a mathematical game of taking objects from heaps.

clue.text: Disconcert gunner, Verdun not fully in sight

indicators.note: not fully in sight means the letters lie partly visible inside the words

explanation.surface: A gunner at the battle of Verdun is thrown by not seeing clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdun was a major First World War battle in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve is to rattle or disconcert someone.

clue.text: Member yet to flap about discharge

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the member
to flap means to be agitated, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has still to panic about being discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flap' rearranges YET to ETY, placed 'about' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty is to discharge the contents of something.

clue.text: Many years without it, rebel force receives the French news

indicators.note: receives means the shortened force takes in the next pieces
without means the word it is removed from the rebel force

parts.note: a militia is an irregular, often rebel, armed force
taken as written
le is French for the
N is short for new, so news is two of them

explanation.surface: A rebel army hears French news over many years without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes IT from MILITIA, leaving MILIA, which 'receives' LE and NN.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are thousand-year spans, a great many years.
